# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 3
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 3

---

*[King Gundaphorus commissions Thomas to build a palace. Thomas gives the money to the poor.]*

1. And when the wedding was ended, Abbanes the merchant presented Thomas to King Gundaphorus and said to him: "Lord king, I have found a man who is a carpenter and a builder, as you commanded me."

2. And the king was pleased and said to Thomas: "What is your skill? Can you build me a palace?"

3. And Thomas said to him: "Yes. For this I have come, to build and to do carpenter's work."

4. And the king took him and went out of the city, and they walked for a great distance, and the king showed Thomas a place and said to him: "I want you to build me a palace in this place."

5. And Thomas said: "I will build it. I will build something great."

6. And the king said: "When will the work be begun?"

7. And Thomas said: "I will begin it now and finish it, for this is my work."

8. And the king commissioned him well and commanded him to receive gold and silver from the treasury and all that was needed, and departed to another country.

9. And when the king had departed, Thomas took all the gold and silver and went about the villages and cities, and distributed it to the poor and the sick and clothed the naked, and he said: "The king commanded me to build him a palace. I am indeed building one for him."

10. And he continued doing this for a long time.

11. After some time the king sent a messenger to Thomas to ask how the palace was going, for he wanted news of it.

12. And the messenger came to Thomas and asked him about the palace.

13. And Thomas said to him: "The palace is finished and lacks nothing but the roof."

14. And the king heard this and was glad.

---
*EMET note: The heavenly palace motif — charity to the poor building treasure in heaven (cf. Matt 6:19–21, 19:21) — is one of the central theological ideas of the ATH. Thomas takes literally the promise of "treasure in heaven" by giving away the earthly funds.*
